title: Edmund and the Deadline
premise: Isandro Nystrom, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by an operation she can't fully remember, is approached by a stranger named Edmund who claims she saved his life years ago—a favor she has no memory of doing. As Edmund calls in the debt, dragging her into a campaign against the covert training network that shaped and then discarded her, Isandro discovers her missing memories were surgically taken, not lost. Torn between loyalty to the handlers who still hold leverage over her old colleagues and the truth Edmund keeps feeding her, she must decide who to betray. In the end, Isandro burns the network's archive, exposes its directors, and chooses a fragile new belonging with Edmund—accepting that some of what she lost will never come back.
about_author: August Coldharbour is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade adjacent to the security world before turning to fiction. Coldharbour writes thrillers about people whose institutions failed them, from a farmhouse office with unreliable internet.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Isandro, working dead-end contract gigs in Lisbon, is cornered at a café by Edmund, who thanks her for saving his life in Prague—an event she cannot recall. He leaves a burner phone and a warning: they're watching her again. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Zero References
chapters.summary: A flashback-tinged chapter tracing Isandro's dismissals from three agencies, each exit tied to gaps in her memory and a sealed incident file. Her former mentor, Voss, calls offering 'reinstatement' if she reports on Edmund. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into suspicion about what was actually done to her.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Edmund explains the debt: someone in the network—the Meridian Group—pulled strings to keep Isandro free after the incident, and now he's collecting on their behalf. He shows her a photo of herself in Prague she doesn't remember being in. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: charm masking urgency; he knows more than he says.

chapters.title: The Night She Doesn't Sleep Through
chapters.summary: Isandro's apartment is searched while she's out; nothing stolen except a decade of her own case notes. She realizes the network never let her go—it was maintaining her. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: violation; invisibility revealed as captivity.

chapters.title: Voss's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Dinner with Voss, who dangles reinstatement and subtly threatens her old colleague Priya, still inside the system. Voss mentions Prague unprompted—and gets one detail wrong. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the mentor mask slips; loyalty begins to rot.

chapters.title: Prague, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Edmund walks Isandro through the Prague operation using documents, photos, and a witness statement. The timeline shows she acted heroically—then someone erased it and burned three analysts as cover. POV: alternating Isandro/Edmund. Emotional beat: vertigo; grief for a self she can't access.

chapters.title: Priya
chapters.summary: Isandro secretly contacts Priya, now a mid-level Meridian officer, under pretext of a job reference. Priya warns her off, terrified—but slips a codeword that matches something in Edmund's files. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: fear and buried loyalty; the first ally inside the walls.

chapters.title: The Training House
chapters.summary: Edmund takes Isandro to a decommissioned facility in the Alentejo where Meridian trained assets—including, the records show, her. She finds her own handwriting in an old logbook dated after her supposed dismissal. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: horror of recognition; belonging weaponized.

chapters.title: What Edmund Isn't Saying
chapters.summary: Isandro cross-checks Edmund's story and finds holes: his Prague rescue doesn't match the witness statement. She confronts him; he admits he wasn't the man she saved—he was the handler who ordered the erasure before defecting. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: betrayal, then wary recalibration; the debt is real but so is his guilt.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Meridian makes contact through Voss: full restoration of her record and memories in exchange for delivering Edmund. They return one recovered memory fragment as proof—which shows Edmund present at her erasure. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by rage; every offer is a hook.

chapters.title: The Fragment
chapters.summary: Isandro interrogates the returned memory all night: it shows her volunteering for the erasure to protect someone—Priya. The incident wasn't her failure; it was her sacrifice, repurposed against her. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: devastating reframe; loyalty was the trap all along.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro and Edmund map Meridian's structure: seven directors, an archive vault in Vienna holding original unredacted files, and a cleanup team already tracking them. They have roughly nine days before the archive is purged. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the deadline becomes real.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Isandro meets Priya in a train station and tells her the truth about the sacrifice. Priya, shaken, agrees to pull Vienna access credentials—but refuses to leave the network yet. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh between two friends.

chapters.title: Ambush in Porto
chapters.summary: A routine document handoff becomes a Meridian ambush; Edmund is captured covering Isandro's escape. The cleanup team leader, Sable, offers Isandro a walk-away window—one day—if she disappears for good. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused; no more running.

chapters.title: One Day
chapters.summary: With hours to vanish, Isandro instead goes to Voss and pretends to accept the counteroffer, buying access codes and learning the purge schedule moves up—to tomorrow night. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the gambler's calm; she stops asking permission to exist.

chapters.title: Vienna, After Hours
chapters.summary: Using Priya's credentials, Isandro infiltrates the Vienna archive during a director's reception upstairs. She locates the vault but triggers a silent lockdown; Sable is waiting inside, expecting her. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread at the threshold; the trap within the plan.

chapters.title: Sable's Version
chapters.summary: Sable argues Meridian protected Isandro when no one else would—that the network is family, flawed but necessary. Isandro stalls, copying the archive to a drive hidden in the vault's maintenance panel. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: seductive ideology; belonging offered one last time.

chapters.title: Burn It Down
chapters.summary: Edmund escapes custody and causes a diversion that forces Sable to choose between stopping Isandro and saving the directors' exposure files. Isandro initiates the purge-reversal: the archive uploads to journalists worldwide. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax; irreversible commitment to truth over safety.

chapters.title: The Directors' Long Night
chapters.summary: As exposures cascade, Meridian fractures: two directors flee, one suicides, Voss goes dark after sending Isandro a single word—'run.' Priya finally defects, bringing the last internal ledger. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: collapse of the institution; vindication shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Sable corners Isandro one final time—not to kill her, but to deliver Meridian's last message: her original memories exist, held privately, and can be hers if she ever asks. Isandro declines, for now. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: quiet power; she refuses to be defined by what was taken.

chapters.title: What the Debt Was For
chapters.summary: Edmund confesses the whole design: his 'debt' story was engineered to reach her because she was the only analyst who'd flagged Meridian's abuses before her erasure. She forgives him—or decides to live alongside it. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: reckoning; trust rebuilt on honesty rather than myth.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Months later, Isandro and Edmund live quietly under new names; the published files have forced hearings. She sleeps a full night for the first time since the incident, wakes, and writes down the memory fragments she chooses to keep. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging chosen, not assigned.
